input: It is important to note that shell-and-tube exchangers play a crucial role in refinery preheat trains, and the unit considered here, which heats crude oil, provides a useful illustration of how design data and operating data are brought together in practice. The exchanger in question handles a substantial thermal duty of 1925 kW. On the hot side of the unit, the stream enters at a temperature of 150 °C and leaves at 110 °C, while on the cold side the crude oil enters at 35 °C and is heated up to 55 °C. When all of these terminal temperatures are taken into account, it is possible to calculate the log-mean temperature difference, which comes out at 84.6 K, thereby providing a measure of the effective driving force for heat transfer across the unit as a whole. Furthermore, the installed heat-transfer area of the exchanger is 55.7 m2, and when this area is combined with the duty and with the log-mean temperature difference, an overall heat-transfer coefficient of 408 W m-2 K-1 is obtained, shedding light on the thermal performance of the unit in its installed condition. It should also be noted that the assessment of fouling was based on a single 90-day run, and, notably, no cleaning cycle has yet been completed, which means that the longer-term picture, including how performance develops over time and how the unit responds once cleaning has taken place, remains incomplete at this stage.
target: A shell-and-tube exchanger heats crude oil in a refinery preheat train. Duty is 1925 kW, with the hot stream cooled from 150 °C to 110 °C and the crude oil heated from 35 °C to 55 °C. The log-mean temperature difference for these terminal temperatures is 84.6 K. The log-mean temperature difference is the mean driving force for heat transfer along the exchanger: the local driving force varies from end to end as the streams approach each other in temperature, and the log-mean value is the single difference that, used with the installed area, reproduces the duty. Installed area is 55.7 m2, and area, duty and the log-mean temperature difference together give an overall coefficient of 408 W m-2 K-1. The overall coefficient states the installed performance directly, as the heat transferred per unit area per kelvin of mean driving force, with the wall and both films folded into the one figure. A coefficient stated on this basis can be compared directly with a later test of the same unit at the same terminal temperatures, and a lower value on retest is the signature of added resistance in the unit, since the area and the streams are unchanged. Fouling was assessed from a single 90-day run, and no cleaning cycle has been completed. The fouling state after cleaning, and the rate at which fouling returns once the unit is back in service, are not covered by the assessment, so the state of the unit over a longer campaign rests on a test that has not yet been made.
